axes.x: easting relative to Elevador Lacerda origin
axes.z: northing relative to Elevador Lacerda origin
axes.y: elevation relative to local vertical datum

osm.notes: Complete versioned OSM bbox snapshot is active for the project perimeter. Derived runtime vectors contain all configured critical roads; live OSM remains refresh/debug only.

conderContours.notes: Official CONDER 1992 contour snapshot is versioned for the project envelope and derives the persistent 2.5 m terrain grid. Runtime live refresh is fallback-only when the persistent product is unavailable.

salvadorMunicipalCartography.notes: Prefer municipal MDT/LiDAR for final terrain when a stable public download or service endpoint for the project tile is identified.

terrainDerivation.notes: CONDER contour elevations are fixed constraints. Unknown grid cells are initialized from nearest contour cells and solved by harmonic relaxation.

vectorDerivation.notes: Road centerlines and polygons are clipped to the project perimeter. Indoor highway features remain excluded from terrain-road derivation. Indoor highway=corridor features are preserved in a separate elevatedCorridors collection so structures such as the Elevador Lacerda upper bridge remain available without being draped onto terrain. Road width provenance follows explicit OSM width first, then integer OSM lanes × 3 m as an estimated carriageway width, then the highway-class fallback. Explicit OSM width/height tags are preserved; all derived widths remain marked estimated. Complete coverage requires every critical road name to be present.

buildingBlockoutPolicy.notes: Automatic building volumes require a real OSM footprint plus explicit height or building:levels-derived height. Footprints crossing more than 0.75 m of terrain relief are skipped for manual foundation/model handling. A footprint that overlaps the rendered road/junction surface expanded by 0.15 m is preserved as source data but is not promoted to a collidable 3D blockout.

elevatedCorridorPolicy.notes: Indoor OSM corridors are rendered as elevated walkable decks. Their horizontal path comes from OSM; the deck datum is anchored to the highest terrain endpoint outside protected structure footprints so the bridge is not draped down the escarpment.

rasterReference.purpose: runtime alignment/debug reference only; not a source of 3D geometry

liveTerrainPreview.notes: Browser preview grid with 4 m spacing and 2 m contour constraints. It may replace the procedural fallback during a session but never promotes itself to geospatial/derived terrain. Persistent terrain remains the higher-resolution 2.5 m product.

roadSurfacePolicy.notes: Gameplay road mesh follows OSM centerlines and active terrain. Longitudinal grading uses a raise-only constrained profile capped at 14% whenever crossfall and total support remain within policy; profiles that exceed support capacity or destabilize a connected junction fall back conservatively and are explicitly audited. The older 0.12 m local smoothing remains only on fallback segments and never cuts below official terrain. Crossfall is capped at 6% by preserving the higher terrain edge and raising only the lower edge. Where this creates more than 0.18 m of support, a terrain-connected retaining skirt is rendered; automatic road fill is limited to 12 m. Compatible road endpoints receive a junction deck fitted to their graded road-edge elevations, capped at 14% plane slope. Junction terrain is masked only beneath the deck using an inset footprint plus adaptive boundary refinement, allowing at most 0.75 m local cut and 3 m local fill, with a perimeter retaining/cut wall; junction-to-road edge mismatch must remain <= 0.15 m. These are rendering/gameplay constraints, not surveyed civil-engineering elevations.

publicSpaceSurfacePolicy.notes: Walkable hard-surface polygons are tessellated before terrain draping so collision triangles do not bridge across terrain relief. Generic leisure=park polygons without an explicit hard surface do not receive an invented paving overlay; the official terrain remains visible and walkable. Source polygon boundaries remain unchanged.

terrainQualityPolicy.notes: Persistent official terrain must preserve the 2.5 m grid or better, retain broad contour coverage, converge below 2 mm solver delta and represent meaningful Cidade Baixa/Cidade Alta relief. These thresholds validate the derived product, not the source survey accuracy.

terrainStructureMaskPolicy.notes: Verified structure footprints mask terrain render/collision only inside their measured volume. Boundary refinement keeps the cut tight to the footprint instead of deleting coarse 2.5 m terrain triangles around the structure.

terrainRenderMaskPolicy.notes: Terrain triangles are adaptively subdivided only where they cross a render-mask boundary. Boundary leaves are refined to at most 8 cm before removal, preserving the original terrain grid away from masks while preventing metre-scale holes around structures and road junction decks.
